summary: A line on the shared workboard says the follow-up work on the app's smart guesses has landed and three more gap designs are claimed.

The last screen of Get started no longer says "Small changes help" when the plan only carries a small part of your spending. It now uses the same rule as the Dashboard: that line only appears when the plan covers 85% or more of the spending, otherwise it says "Check the numbers first" and links to what the answer rests on. The Next best action page also rounded a guessed left-over to the nearest $10, like the other pages, instead of showing "about $301".
points: Same 85% rule as the Dashboard
"Check the numbers first" links to the figures behind the answer
A figure resting on our guesses is rounded to the nearest $10 everywhere
numbers: 85% of spending carried is the cutoff

summary: When your retirement money runs out early, the app now asks you to check the numbers it rests on before changing anything. Your plan's "What would help" and a new Needs attention item open those numbers on the page that shows whether the money will last. If the plan already covers 85% or more of your spending, the item sits under Fine for now and is not counted.
points: New Needs attention item, for example "Your retirement money runs out at 65"
It points to the 7 numbers the answer rests on
The Dashboard says "Small changes help" only when the plan carries 85% or more of spending

summary: When you chat with Ask, any balance or goal amount the app filled in for you is now marked "(our guess)" before it reaches the assistant. The assistant is told what the mark means and to say so whenever it uses one. Ask no longer passes our guess off as your own figure.
points: Guessed balances and goal amounts carry the mark
The assistant must say when it relies on a guess

summary: On the Expenses page, the card that offers to fill in numbers for you no longer offers a blank home or college goal beside your spending. It now offers the spending alone under "Not sure what you spend?", and tapping it writes nothing else. The goal amounts stay on the Dashboard card and on Our guesses for you.
points: Tap writes only the spending
Goal amounts stay where you can review them

summary: A new plan no longer gets "Look over the assumptions" next to the checklist's "Look over our guesses", which said nearly the same thing. A year after your last look, or after the plan was made, the Housekeeping list asks once: "Once a year: look over the assumptions". It is never an amber check and never counted.
points: No duplicate reminder on a new plan
Yearly reminder lives under Housekeeping
Never counts against you

summary: A goal whose amount was left blank is no longer called "on track". Your plan and the Dashboard's Goals tile now say "1 needs an amount", and a goal behind on an amount we filled in says so calmly. Only a goal behind on your own amount shows amber. The Goals page marks our amount as "Our guess for now: tap to type yours".
points: Blank amount shows "needs an amount"
Amber only for your own amounts
Goals page labels our guesses plainly
Your plan and the Dashboard use one shared line

summary: On the Dashboard and Your plan, each figure that is still waiting now says what it waits for: your pay, your spending, or both, in the same words as Get started, and tapping it opens that question. A short month based on our guess of your pay is no longer shown as a red overspend. Goal amounts left blank get a quiet card after the money tiles, and Your plan lists the month's guesses first, pay then spending.
points: Left-over row names what it waits for
Pay is asked first when it is our guess
No red overspend from a guessed pay
Retirement and cushion rows say what they need

summary: A line on the shared workboard says the plain-words round of the smart guesses work has landed, its claim is released and notes are left for other pages.
